title: ISSM: review and apply an Auto-config setting
chapter_timing: Receipt-bound logical chapters include control cue, actual transition and confirmation; durations are video times.

steps.title: Goal and prerequisites
instructions: Open CryoLauncher with a verified BYO AWS connection. Configure your MATLAB license and connect the same-owner Connector.
Choose Cloud and ISSM SquareIceShelf. This guide changes only the stressbalance maximum-iteration setting.
steps.why: Use the reviewed BYO workflow for one native ISSM solver change.
steps.expected: Example: canonical SquareIceShelf; stressbalance iteration cap 120.
steps.note: Auto-config prepares a configuration; Create plan and Apply to configuration do not submit a native job.

steps.title: 1. Describe a single change
instructions: Choose Auto-config · Beta.
Enter exactly: Set stressbalance max iterations to 120.
steps.why: A narrow request makes the proposed change easy to verify.
steps.expected: Keep the model, example and Cloud execution mode.

steps.title: 2. Create and review the proposal
instructions: Choose Create plan.
Review the Stressbalance max iterations row. Proposed must be 120; retain ISSM · SquareIceShelf · Cloud.
steps.why: A plan proposes a change; it does not start the solver.

steps.title: 3. Apply the reviewed setting
instructions: Scroll to the proposal and choose Apply to configuration.
Wait for Configuration updated and 1 setting changed.
steps.why: Apply only after confirming 120 and the retained experiment.
steps.note: The accepted staged helper later set md.stressbalance.maxiter = 120 before the native solve.

steps.title: 4. Return to the native form
instructions: Choose Review in Advanced to inspect the native controls.
Review the existing model and run controls before launching.
In Experiment confirm Model ISSM and Examples SquareIceShelf.
Keep Action Run and Run target runme.m.
steps.why: The native form is where you review execution controls. The change should not select a different scientific example. runme.m retains the canonical scientific entrypoint.
steps.expected: The native canonical entrypoint is retained.
steps.note: Canonical Square.par remains unchanged: hmax 1000 m and hmin 300 m. The recorded case retained two requested MPI processes and the qualified image pin.

steps.title: 7. Review the native cloud plan
instructions: Open Review & Launch. Confirm ISSM and SquareIceShelf.
Review your resource and time-limit settings and the cost estimate in your own account.
In the expanded review, scroll to Infrastructure.
Check Account, Storage, Container image and Compute readiness.
steps.why: Review before submitting so the new run uses the intended example. Storage, image, license and compute must be ready before submission.
steps.expected: Account, storage, image and compute must be ready.
steps.note: The accepted run used 2 vCPU and 8 GiB. An estimate is not an invoice or a spending cap. Read the review before the separate explicit launch action.

steps.title: 9. Submit explicitly
instructions: Scroll to the bottom of the review. Read the final notice.
Choose Launch cloud run. Stay on the page while staging begins.
Check that the new Cloud run names SquareIceShelf.
Follow this selected run until Completed; startup and model execution are separate periods.
steps.why: This explicit action starts the native cloud execution. Follow the new run before inspecting its outputs.
steps.expected: The current run changes from staging to submitting.
steps.note: Create plan and Apply did not submit this job. Recorded startup 212.717 s; Batch task 41.369 s; total submission-to-stop 254.086 s.

steps.title: 11. Select the native field
instructions: For the completed Auto-config run open View results or Results.
Select StressbalanceSolution and field Vel.
Choose Render after selecting Vel.
Read the field summary and colorbar; the accepted mesh has 91 vertices and 148 triangles.
steps.why: The selected field must belong to the completed run. Render updates the displayed field; it does not rerun the solver.
steps.note: The result belongs to the selected run, rather than the current experiment controls on the left.

steps.title: 13. Prepare the result archive
instructions: Scroll below the rendered field and choose Download results.
Wait for a newly prepared results_bundle link. Keep the run selected while packaging.
Choose the fresh download link. Save the ZIP with your run record.
The accepted archive contains the neutral mesh, native fields, exact figure and runtime/RNG provenance.
steps.why: Package the mesh, fields, figure and runtime provenance together. The fresh link saves the archive prepared for this run.
steps.expected: Keep the native outputs and runtime provenance together.

steps.title: 15. Interpret this result
instructions: Open figures/StressbalanceSolution_Vel.png from the saved archive.
This recorded solve converged in 23 iterations; 120 is an upper limit, not a request for 120 iterations.
steps.why: The colorbar and solver record explain the result in physical units.
steps.expected: ISSM converged in 23 iterations, below both caps of 100 and 120.
steps.note: Actual runtime: MATLAB R2024b Update 7; ISSM 2026.1. The canonical domain is 1000 km × 1000 km.

steps.title: 16. Read the qualification
instructions: The staged override and native log prove that 120 was applied before solve.
The mesh, Pressure, Vel, Vx, Vy and iteration count exactly matched the accepted Basic retake.
steps.why: Convergence below both caps explains this unchanged recorded result.
steps.expected: For this changed-cap case, every compared numeric value was exactly equal.
steps.note: This is one changed-cap comparison, consistent with convergence below either cap; it is not a general accuracy or reproducibility claim.
